question.text: When the spot price of Nifty is 17,500 and a trader holds a call option with strike price 17,500, the option is:

answer.text: At-the-Money (ATM) because the spot price equals the strike price
In-the-Money (ITM) because the option has been purchased
Out-of-the-Money (OTM) because there is no profit
Neither ITM nor OTM - it is called a neutral option

explanation.text: The Logic: When the spot price equals the strike price, the option is At-the-Money (ATM). This applies to both calls and puts, so a 17,500 call with spot at 17,500 is ATM. The Trap: ATM does not mean 'no profit'. An ATM option still has time value because there is uncertainty about where the spot will be at expiry, so it can still become profitable. Note: For an ATM option, intrinsic value is zero and the entire premium is time value.
